newsitem.title: RUSSIA: MICEX to start futures dollar, T-bill trading.
newsitem.headline: MICEX to start futures dollar, T-bill trading.

text.p: The Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) will start futures trading in dollars and Treasury bills on Thursday, a MICEX spokesman said on Monday.
He gave no other details but said a news conference on futures trading will be held on Friday.
In February MICEX said it would trade currency contracts running in months for up to 12 months, based on $1,000 and 1,000 mark lots.

T-bill contracts would be based on the secondary market price of six-month paper one month before the bills mature, with contracts running in months up to five months. Lots would be 100 million roubles.
MICEX intended to start futures trading in March but the start was postponed at the central bank's request as the regulatory background had not been fully prepared.
Central bank first deputy chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said the central bank and MICEX had had to change some procedures, agree on the interpretation of some terms and resolve accountancy problems.
"Today we have all the necessary documents and, what is the most important, procedures for the futures market to work," he told Reuters.
Some smaller Russian exchanges already trade dollar and T-bill futures, but volumes are low.
MICEX is the official trading centre for T-bills, and until this summer was used by the central bank to set official dollar/rouble rates.
